messages.subject: Re: Binomial count data
parts:
> > I use point transect to estimate densities of songbirds. I have grouped
> > the data into binomial count data (birds occuring within 30 meters and
> > birds occuring outside 30 meters) as in Bibby et al. 1985. As I run the
> > analysis, I get the message "the number of intervals are less than the
> > number of key parameters" How do I treat binomial counts in Distance
> > 3.5?

You can only fit one parameter models to binomial data. Thus you could
fit the half-normal key with no adjustments (recommended), or the uniform
key with one adjustment. You cannot fit the hazard-rate model using
DISTANCE. Alternatively, you can fit the half-normal model using the
equation given for binomial data in the distance sampling book (see
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distancebook/ ).
